candidates.statement: Primary users are viewers who are able to choose various things to watch videos.
candidates.modality: descriptive (role definition)

evidence_candidates.quote: the primary users are gonna be so viewers. So people who are able to choose various things to watch videos and the like

candidates.statement: Primary users also include streamers who share content with the platform.
candidates.modality: descriptive (role definition)

evidence_candidates.quote: perhaps streamers where somebody who's going to share, content with the platform

candidates.statement: Platform must make sure that some viewers cannot see certain things that are not suitable for all viewers.
candidates.modality: must ('we'll have to make sure')
context: content that is not suitable for all viewers

evidence_candidates.quote: we'll have to make sure that a some viewers can't see certain things

candidates.statement: Some kinds of content should not be allowed to be shared by streamers with anybody.
candidates.modality: prohibition ('should not be allowed')

evidence_candidates.quote: there's some sorts of content that streamers should not be allowed to share with anybody

candidates.statement: Content with explicit language is an instance that the platform should be careful about.
candidates.modality: caution ('you might want to be careful')
context: example given for the prohibited content

evidence_candidates.quote: things with explicit language, for instance

candidates.statement: A large company hosts the videos on its servers and controls what is uploaded and what is taken away to the viewer.
candidates.modality: belief about how such platforms work ('I think in most cases')

evidence_candidates.quote: they're going to be the ones who get to manage and control what's uploaded

candidates.statement: As a viewer, it is essential to get a specific type of video or content by searching via text.
candidates.modality: essential

evidence_candidates.quote: I think it's essential to be able to try to get a specific type of video or content by searching via text

candidates.statement: Viewer can also get a specific type of content by using filters of some sort.
candidates.modality: tentative alternative ('or perhaps')

evidence_candidates.quote: or perhaps by filters of some sort

candidates.statement: Viewer can search visually by seeing a large volume of different options and clicking through them.
candidates.modality: want ('I would like to be able to')

evidence_candidates.quote: to be able to search visually, so I would like to be able to see a large volume of different options and click through it

candidates.statement: Streamer or uploader has an option to create, upload a video or start a stream.
candidates.modality: want ('I would want to see some option')

evidence_candidates.quote: I would want to see some option where I could go and create to upload a video or start a stream

candidates.statement: Uploader can put a description into the video and add a transcript or captions.

evidence_candidates.quote: put some sort of description in, add, perhaps a transcript captions of the like

candidates.statement: Uploader can edit the video, adding sound effects, trimming and cropping.
candidates.modality: strong preference ('would be very useful')

evidence_candidates.quote: would be to edit those. So I can add sound effects. Trim crop

candidates.statement: Searching with vague criteria should still get meaningful results.
candidates.modality: want ('I want to be able to')

evidence_candidates.quote: I want to be able to search, using vague criteria, but that should still get me meaningful results

candidates.statement: The content should be received on the viewer's machine in a reasonable way, without freezing constantly, as a seamless stream of buffered data.
candidates.modality: want/avoid ('I don't want it to freeze', 'I want')

evidence_candidates.quote: I don't want it to freeze constantly. I want a seamless stream of buffered data

candidates.statement: The viewer uses these platforms for entertainment purposes and for education purposes.
candidates.modality: personal usage statement

evidence_candidates.quote: I would use these sorts of platforms as a viewer for entertainment purposes and for education purposes

candidates.statement: Viewer wants to gain information quickly by a quick search instead of reading a book.
candidates.modality: want ('I want to gain information')

evidence_candidates.quote: I want to gain information. So I don't wanna read a book. I want to have a quick search

candidates.statement: When uploading an existing video, the creator must be sure their formats are compatible with the system.

candidates.statement: The creator must be sure there are no length requirements.
candidates.modality: obstacle hypothesis ('there might be some technical complications')

candidates.statement: Publishing the uploaded video to the web should be a simple process.
candidates.modality: question raising concern ('Is that a simple process?')

evidence_candidates.quote: How do they actually publish that to the web? Is that a simple process?

candidates.statement: The creator should not have to sit and wait for the whole video to be uploaded before publication.
candidates.modality: question raising concern ('Do they have to sit and wait...')

evidence_candidates.quote: Do they have to sit and wait for the whole video to be published or uploaded before publication

candidates.statement: Hovering over a thumbnail shows a small snippet of the content.

candidates.statement: Video cards show the creator, which links to the account, plus statistics such as views and creation date.

candidates.statement: The upload/publish form asks for a file, a title, a description and other information such as languages, then a publish action.

candidates.modality: reported compliance requirement ('are asked to give 24 h notice')

candidates.statement: Viewers can add things to their watch list.

candidates.statement: The stakeholder wants to talk about actually watching a video and what the options there might be.
